records.name: Pennsylvania SPCA (PSPCA)
records.summary: A large animal shelter and rescue with a Philadelphia headquarters on Erie Avenue. It places animals in foster homes and welcomes adult volunteers for animal care, adoption events and special events.
records.what_you_do: Volunteers socialize dogs and cats, help at adoption and special events, or support office work. Foster homes care for animals until they are adopted, and the shelter provides food, supplies and vet care at no cost.

first_step.how: Pick a location on the volunteer page and apply online through Volgistics. Volunteers must be 18 or older and able to work with minimal supervision once trained.
first_step.basis: The public page explains how to apply and lists several roles, but it does not describe the training length or time commitment.

records.notes: The foster page covers several foster types, a foster support manager, and free supplies and vet care. Protective custody fosters must have fostered before, live in Pennsylvania and pass a background check. The foster email is the foster team's address; no general volunteer email or phone is published. Volunteers must be at least 18 and able to handle animal dander and cleaning chemicals. The shelter's other centers (Main Line, Lancaster, Danville) are outside the city.

records.name: Morris Animal Refuge
records.summary: A Center City animal welfare group, founded in 1874, that runs adoptions, a community cat program and a Philly pets program. Its website also has sections for foster homes and volunteers.
records.what_you_do: The website has separate Foster and Volunteer sections. This read did not reach their details, so check them before signing up.

schedule.text: Adoption hours are Tuesday and Saturday noon to 5 pm, and Wednesday and Friday noon to 7 pm.

first_step.how: Use the Volunteer or Foster section of the website, or email info@morrisanimalrefuge.org
first_step.basis: Public volunteer and foster sections and a general email are listed, but the steps and minimum age were not read.

records.notes: Dated posts on the homepage run from August 21 to September 28, 2026. The homepage adoption counter shows 0 for 2026 and was not used. Foster and volunteer pages were linked but not read, so roles and requirements are unknown.

records.name: Street Tails Animal Rescue (STAR)
records.summary: A Philadelphia dog rescue that cares for overlooked dogs in a kennel facility, places them in adoptive homes, and asks for foster homes and adult volunteers.
records.what_you_do: The website has a Foster Application and an Adult Volunteer Application. The page did not describe the roles, so ask what the work involves.

schedule.text: Office hours are Tuesday to Saturday 11 am to 5 pm and Sunday noon to 5 pm. Closed Monday. Visits to dogs are by appointment only.

first_step.how: Apply through the Foster Application or Adult Volunteer Application on the website, or call or email the rescue.
first_step.basis: Public foster and volunteer applications are listed, but the page does not explain the steps or time commitment.

records.notes: The site shows a 2022 footer and has no dated posts, so the status is probably_active but not confirmed. The Hound-O-Ween event has no date. The foster and volunteer application pages were not read. Older 2019 pet-of-the-week items seen only in search results are not used. Fee information is not published.

records.name: Green Street Rescue
records.summary: A nonprofit cat rescue in Brewerytown that runs Le Cat Café, where visitors can spend time with adoptable cats, and places cats with foster homes until they are adopted.
records.what_you_do: Foster a cat until it is adopted, or visit the cafe to meet the cats. The site says many people volunteer but does not list volunteer roles.

schedule.text: Cafe hours: Sunday 10 am to 6 pm, Monday, Tuesday and Thursday 11 am to 6 pm, Friday 11 am to 7 pm, Saturday 10 am to 7 pm. Closed Wednesday.

cost.text: Adoption is $140 for one cat or $200 for two. Volunteer and cafe visit costs are not shown on the site.

first_step.how: Fill out the foster application linked on the site. The rescue checks references and your vet before approving, then connects approved fosters with a cat, usually picked up at the cafe.
first_step.basis: Anyone can book a cafe visit to meet the cats, while fostering needs an approved application.

records.notes: The site shows a 2022 copyright footer and no dated news, so the status is probably_active but not confirmed. Phone and email are not published on the site; the contact page is linked but was not read. The site lists a TNRM program and a barn cat program, which were not read in detail.

records.name: KittenSnatchers
records.summary: A volunteer-led nonprofit founded in 2020 that rescues Philadelphia's stray cats and kittens and places them in foster homes until they find adoptive homes.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer as a temporary host to care for a stray cat or kitten in your home, or apply to foster through the online forms on the website.

cost.text: The standard adoption fee is not published on the group's site.

first_step.how: Fill in the temporary host form or the foster form linked on the website.
first_step.basis: Public online forms for hosting and fostering are linked, but the page does not describe screening or support.

records.notes: Conflict: a WeRescue directory listing gives a physical address (164 Sigel Street) and a phone number, but the group's own site says it has no physical location. Neither the address nor the phone number is published here. The Clear the Shelters adoption campaign ran August 1 to 31, 2026. The adoption process and fostering pages were linked but not read.

records.name: Seger Dog Park (Seger Park Dog Owners Association)
records.summary: A dog park in Washington Square West run by a nonprofit dog owners association. It organizes community cleanups and events, and asks for memberships and donations to pay for upkeep.
records.what_you_do: Join the association's cleanup efforts and community events, or become a member to help pay for upkeep. The site says cleanups keep litter off streets and out of waterways.

first_step.how: Email the association at the address on the website, or use the membership link on the site.
first_step.basis: The site lists an email and a membership link, but the membership price and cleanup sign-up steps were not shown.

records.notes: The site footer reads 2019, and the calendar page showed no dated events, so the status is probably_active with low confidence. Entry rules and the membership price are not shown. A 2021 newspaper piece describing the park as volunteer-run was seen only in search results and is not used. A 2016 Philadelphia magazine list gives 1020 Lombard Street, but the group's own site gives 1001 Rodman Street, which is used here. A summer concert series called Woofstock is mentioned without dates.

records.name: Palmer Doggie Depot
records.summary: A free, volunteer-run dog park in Fishtown. The New Kensington Community Development Corporation built it at the Shissler Recreation Center, and it asks visitors for donations to keep it open.
records.what_you_do: Help keep the park running as a volunteer. The site links to two sign-up pages, Join Our Pack and Join the Bark Rangers, which were not read, so the roles are unknown.

cost.text: Free for all dogs and their owners. Donations are requested to keep the park open.

first_step.how: Use the Join Our Pack or Join the Bark Rangers link on the website, or email the group.
first_step.basis: The park is free and open to the public, and the site has sign-up links and an email, but those pages were not read.

records.notes: The site says there is no attendant on duty and visitors use the park at their own risk. The address comes from a 2016 Philadelphia magazine list, not from the group's own site. The site has no dated posts, so the status is probably_active but not confirmed. Hours and phone are not published.

records.name: Roxborough Dog Park
records.summary: A members-only dog park in Roxborough run by a nonprofit association with a volunteer board. Every member is asked to volunteer at the park.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer at the park, as every member must, and attend the association's open community meetings. The site does not list meeting dates.

schedule.text: The park is open every day from 6:30 am to 9 pm.

cost.text: $25 per quarter or $100 per year, as published.

first_step.how: Apply through the Apply Now links on the membership page. Applicants are screened before they are accepted.
first_step.basis: Membership needs an application, a screening and a fee before you can see the park.

records.notes: The footer reads 2020 and no dated events are shown, so the status is probably_active with low confidence. The site says the community calendar and news sections have no dated entries. A link on the activities page points to an unrelated template domain, which was not followed. No phone number is published.

records.name: Northwestern Stables
records.summary: A riding stable in Wissahickon Valley Park that teaches group lessons year round to children over 7 and adults, runs summer day camps, and holds shows and fundraisers that welcome volunteer help.
records.what_you_do: Take group riding lessons placed by level, go to summer camp, or help with a schooling show fundraiser through the volunteer sign-up sheet. The stable also runs Racehorse Restarts, which rehabilitates retired racehorses.

schedule.text: Year-round group lessons for children over 7 and adults, plus summer day camps for ages 7 to 13. Dated events on the site: Haunted Horses on October 24, 2026 at 4:30 pm, and Holiday Horses and Bazaar on December 5, 2026 at 10 am.

cost.text: Prices are not published on the site.

first_step.how: Call (215) 242-8892 or use the contact on the website to ask about lessons, camps and volunteering.
first_step.basis: Lessons are open to children over 7 and adults and are placed by level, with a phone number listed, but the site does not say beginners are welcome.

records.notes: Legal status is not stated on the site. The name includes Inc. and the site asks for donations, which suggests a nonprofit, but this is not confirmed. Facebook posts show relative dates and were not used. A Fall Schooling Show post names a Sunday, September 27 with no year, so it is not used as evidence. Photos on the site are placeholders.

records.name: Gerald B. Shreiber Pet Therapy Program at CHOP
records.summary: A pet therapy program at the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia. Trained volunteers and their dogs visit patients in the hospital.
records.what_you_do: Bring your own registered dog to visit patients at least once a month, in two-hour shifts, going room to room with the program coordinator's guidance.

cost.text: CHOP Volunteer Services covers health clearances and background checks, and dog screening is free to the owner. Other costs are not stated.

first_step.how: Send the program's interview request through the web form on its page. Applicants have an in-person interview without the dog, then dog screening, health clearances, background checks and a two-hour orientation.
first_step.basis: An interview, dog screening, clearances, background checks and an orientation all come before the first visit, and the page says no exemptions are offered.

records.notes: Dogs must be 1 to 10 years old and registered with Alliance of Therapy Dogs, Bright and Beautiful Therapy Dogs, Comfort Caring Canines or Pet Partners. The only dated item read is a September 2019 article, so the status rests on the program page being current. No exact tag for therapy dog work exists in the animals family, so hospital_volunteering is used. The program page gives no team count; a 2019 article cites 60 teams.

records.name: Citizens for a No-Kill Philadelphia
records.summary: A nonprofit that works to save healthy and treatable pets in Philadelphia shelters. It runs free community pet food pantries and helps owners find rescues instead of surrendering pets.
records.what_you_do: Help at pet pantry and community outreach events. The site lists no volunteer roles or sign-up steps, so ask the group how to help.

locations.label: Pet pantry and outreach events across Philadelphia

cost.text: The community pet pantries are listed as free.

first_step.how: Email info@phillynokill.org to ask about volunteering or the next pet pantry.
first_step.basis: A public email is listed, but the site does not describe volunteer roles or sign-up.

records.notes: The site has Events and News sections, but the homepage shows no dated items. Shelter volunteering is the closest tag, not a confirmed volunteer role. The mailing address is a PO box in Southeastern, PA (19399), outside the city, and no office is listed. PAWS free pet food pantry listings name this group as a co-host, but those PAWS pages were seen only in search results.

records.name: Pegasus Therapeutic Riding Academy
records.summary: A nonprofit riding center on Bustleton Avenue in Northeast Philadelphia. It offers therapeutic horseback riding for people with disabilities, plus autism, adult, first responder and 4-H programs.
records.what_you_do: Riders take weekly lessons and equine-assisted learning classes. Volunteers help with riders and horses, but volunteer roles were not confirmed from a readable page.
records.notes: The group's own website could not be read: both the bare and www hosts fail with a TLS certificate name mismatch. The record rests on a city page archived in 2022 that lists a horse show on September 30, 2023, which makes the status dormant by the evidence rule. Re-check the website or a dated post before trusting it, and change the status if activity is confirmed. Fees, scholarships and volunteer age and training details are not confirmed. A TeenLife volunteer listing for this group returned HTTP 403 and was not used.

records.name: Stray Cat Relief Fund
records.summary: A nonprofit serving Philadelphia and New Jersey that traps, spays or neuters, vaccinates and returns stray cats, looks after cat colonies, and places cats with foster homes and at a small adoption center.
records.what_you_do: Volunteers trap, transport and care for cats, manage colonies and help at events. The group also lends humane traps to community members. Fosters care for cats until they are adopted.

locations.label: Mailing address (PO box, no walk-in office listed)

first_step.how: Apply through the Volunteer, Fostering or Adoption Application pages linked on the website. Trapping events are also listed.
first_step.basis: Public application pages and trapping events are listed, but the site does not say how new volunteers start.

records.notes: The site gives 2024 figures (138 cats through TNVR and 320 cats adopted in 2024) but no dated news, and its footer reads 2023, so the status is probably_active without an exact month. The three annual events (SCRF Bingo, Caturday Night Fever and The Stray Cat Scurry) have no dates. Foster and volunteer forms were linked but not read. No phone is published. No street address is used because the site gives only a PO box.

notes: Budget: all 10 WebSearch calls used (hard cap reached). About 30 WebFetch calls. Verdicts: 13 publish, 0 hide, 0 duplicate. Fetch failures were per site, not a wide rate limit: Pegasus (certificate mismatch), Orianna Hill (empty text), TeenLife and Petfinder (403). Redirects were not followed when the target was unrelated: qvk9.org redirected to two unrelated domains and phillyfido.org redirected to an unrelated Asheville site, so neither produced a record. Search summaries were not treated as sources unless a page was read, and the search-only facts are left out of the records. KittenSnatchers: a WeRescue directory gives a physical address and phone that the group's own site does not, so neither is published. Pegasus: its own site could not be read, so the record is dormant with low confidence; re-check before trusting it. Status choices for undated working sites (Street Tails, Green Street, Seger, Palmer Doggie Depot, Roxborough, CHOP, Stray Cat Relief Fund, Citizens for a No-Kill Philadelphia) are probably_active with low or medium confidence, because the group's own site is current on contacts or hours but shows no dated items. Tag choices: no therapy dog tag exists in the animals family, so CHOP uses hospital_volunteering; Citizens for a No-Kill Philadelphia uses shelter_volunteering as the closest fit, not a confirmed volunteer role. Not recorded because no own site was read: Saved Me, Save A Yorkie Rescue, Diamonds In The Ruff, Philly Kitty, City Kitties, PAWS for People, Roxy Reading Therapy Dogs, Comfort Caring Canines, New Leash on Life. Not recorded because out of area or out of scope: Forgotten Cats (Willow Grove), Tail Waggin' Tutors (Glenside library), Riding for the Handicapped of Western Pennsylvania (McCandless, near Pittsburgh). Dropped with reason: Delaware Valley Ornithological Club (a wild bird club that belongs with birding, not pet birds; its site was not fetched); Pennsylvania Parrot People (a 2011 forum group with no current evidence). Also seen but not recorded: Monk's Dog Run in Port Richmond (volunteer maintained, no group name on the list), the Market Street dog run (Delaware River Waterfront), and the Dog Park at Bok (no group named on a readable page). PAWS programs (free pet food pantry and TNR vouchers) and PURR, ACCT Philly, Friends of Courtesy Stable, Monastery Stables, Fletcher Street, Work to Ride, PAWS and the Philadelphia Zoo are excluded as already in the directory.
